subject: DPA: residency, retention and deletion - clarifications & proposed language
messages:
From: Tom Bell <tom.bell@finexushealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Finexus Legal <legal@finexushealth.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on DPA residency/retention language (Finexus)

Hi Marissa / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the platform looks promising. Our legal and security teams reviewed the DPA and came back with a short list of clarifications focused on residency, retention, and deletion guarantees. We've attached a sheet (Finexus-DPA-questions.xlsx) with row-level questions, but the high-level asks are: 

- Can Redwood commit to onshore (US) residency for customer data and backups for our account?
- What is the deletion timeline for: (a) active data, (b) snapshots/backups, and (c) logs/telemetry?
- Do you provide a certified deletion manifest and an operational playbook for erasure events?
- How do you handle BYOK / customer-managed keys with respect to deletion and residual copies?

We'd like proposed redline language we can include directly in the DPA; if possible, please provide 2 options (Standard and Enterprise) so our GC can choose. Can you also add any operational constraints (e.g., blackout windows for snapshot deletion) we should be aware of?

Appreciate a quick turnaround as we are aiming to close by month-end.

Best,
Tom Bell
Head of Platform & Security
Finexus Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on DPA residency/retention language (Finexus)

Hi Tom — thanks for the clear list and the attachment. Attaching a short excerpt from our standard DPA (redwood-dpa-snippet.pdf) and a one-page summary of practical options. High-level responses up front: 

1) Residency: We can commit to logical separation and primary storage in the US for your tenant in our hosted product. For backups, we offer an onshore-only option under Dedicated or Private deployments (Enterprise commitment).

2) Deletion timelines: Our standard offering is: active data removed from live storage within 30 days of request; snapshots/backups are scheduled for deletion within 90 days (to allow snapshot reconciliation). Logs and telemetry are defaulted to 180 days but can be reduced for Enterprise with contractual SLA.

3) Certified deletion: We can provide a deletion manifest for enterprise customers as part of our evidence package (PDF manifest + audit trace). For high-assurance customers we offer an on-demand certified erasure report.

4) BYOK: With customer-managed keys, when the key is revoked we consider the data inaccessible. We recommend combining revocation with an operational purge timeline; full cryptographic destruction is subject to our backup retention windows unless we agree to a faster carve-out.

I'll ask Karthik to reply with technical specifics around snapshot lifecycles, and Laura to propose redline language. Attached: redwood-dpa-snippet.pdf.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call (Mon/Tue) to walk through options and land on language for a single redline set.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on DPA residency/retention language (Finexus)

Tom — quick technical clarifications to help your security team: 

- "Snapshots/backups": Our serving runtime takes incremental snapshots for model cache and customer data (application payloads). Snapshots are retained in object storage and referenced by snapshot IDs. Deletion flow: mark -> logical purge -> physical overwrite/GC. The logical purge is immediate; physical reclaim depends on the storage provider and snapshot chain (typ. up to 90 days in the Standard plan).

- "Logs/telemetry": We keep structured telemetry (request/response metadata) separately from payloads. By default 180 days. For Enterprise we can offer 60/90/180 tiers with contract language.

- "Backups in other regions": For the hosted plan, cross-region replication is used for DR; we can disable cross-region backup for a tenant if you opt for onshore-only (applies to Dedicated/Private).

- "BYOK": If you choose BYOK and you destroy the key, the data is unreadable immediately. Note: object-level copies (snapshots) encrypted under different key material may still exist until their lifecycle expires. We can include a contractual commitment to expedite snapshot re-encryption/expiry when BYOK is used, subject to an agreed operational window (we normally propose 30-90 days).

Operational constraints to call out in redline: maintenance blackout windows, snapshot compaction schedule (weekly), and a maximum of one scheduled snapshot deletion job per week per tenant. Those constrain how quickly a snapshot can be fully purged.

Happy to jump on the call.

—Karthik
Principal, Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Bell <tom.bell@finexushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Oct 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA residency/retention language (Finexus)

Tom — thanks for the list. I've drafted two redline proposals and attached them as a single doc (redline_proposal.docx): a "Standard" and an "Enterprise" option. Summary of the proposed language (high level):

Standard (no billing change):
- Residency: Customer data will be stored logically in the US. Backups may be stored in additional regions for DR; we will notify Customer if cross-border copies exist.
- Deletion: Redwood will initiate permanent deletion of Customer Data within 30 days of a deletion request. Snapshots and backups will be marked for deletion immediately and physically purged no later than 90 days after the request.
- Evidence: Redwood will provide a deletion manifest (CSV) within 30 days of completion of purge.

Enterprise (paid commitment):
- Residency: Contractually guaranteed onshore storage for both primary and backup copies.
- Deletion: Active data purge within 14 days; snapshots/backups purged within 30 days.
- Evidence: Certified deletion report (signed PDF), and up to 3 expedited on-demand purge jobs per 12-month period.
- BYOK: If Customer elects BYOK, Redwood will coordinate key revocation with an accelerated purge window of no greater than 30 days for snapshots, subject to operational constraints.

I also added a clause for legal hold: Customer must provide written notice with scope and duration; Redwood will provide a technical overlay for preservation and then resume deletion per agreed timelines after the hold ends.

Please review the redlines and tell me which option you'd prefer or which parts to combine. If Finexus needs different timelines, indicate the sections you want to negotiate and we can run a quick cost/ops estimate.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Laura / Marissa / Karthik — appreciate the thoughtful and specific options. Finexus legal prefers the Enterprise option but we'd like to confirm two small items before we sign: (1) the exact mechanism for the "certified deletion report" (fields included: snapshot IDs, deletion timestamps, storage buckets, and operator signature) and (2) whether the 30-day accelerated purge with BYOK can be made contractual without a manual operational review step (we'd prefer automatic scheduling upon key revocation).

If you can accept those two clarifications as redlines (we can add a short annex specifying the deletion report schema), we'll route for exec approval and ask for a DocuSign. Can we also lock a short mutual action plan in HubSpot so procurement has visibility?

Proposed next step: 30-min call Monday 10/22 to confirm the annex, then we will circulate the DocuSign.

Thanks,
Tom
